stem: In triangle $VWY$, the point $Z$ lies on $VY$ and the point $X$ lies on $WY$, with $ZX\parallel VW$. It is given that $VW={=2*k}$, $ZX={=k}$, $XY={=m}$ and $YZ={=n}$. Determine the length of $WY$.
solution: $ZX\parallel VW$ and $ZX=\frac{1}{2}VW$ (half of ${=2*k}$ is ${=k}$), so $Z$ is the mid-point of $VY$ and $X$ is the mid-point of $WY$.
Since $X$ is the mid-point of $WY$, $WY=2\times XY$ (definition of mid-point).
The length $YZ={=n}$ is not needed to find $WY$.
notes: Modelled on ex7-7-9 and ex7-7-10 (parallel line half the length of the base; deduce that X and Z are mid-points; extra data given that is not needed). The book also gives an angle; it is left out here because a random angle could make the triangle impossible. YZ is kept as the extra datum and is drawn between |m-k|+1 and m+k-1, so triangle YZX (and therefore the doubled triangle YVW) always exists. The answer 2*m is also what similar triangles give (YX/YW = ZX/VW = 1/2), so a solver using either route agrees. The configuration is stated in words (Z on VY, X on WY, ZX parallel to VW) so no figure is needed.
